title: “Warisan at a Crossroads: Identity, Leadership and Electoral Survival” By Vilashini Somiah and Jo-Anna Sue Henley Rampas
summary: This paper examines how Parti Warisan’s future electoral survival and relevance in Malaysia’s sixteenth general election depend on moving beyond charismatic leadership and regional autonomy discourse to build stronger grassroots organisation and form a cohesive federal bargaining bloc.

title: “The Twilight of Reformasi: Freedom of Expression and Civic Engagement in Indonesia and Malaysia” By Iim Halimatusa’diyah and Norshahril Saat
summary: This monograph argues that despite past democratic gains following the fall of authoritarian regimes, both Indonesia and Malaysia are currently experiencing a decline in freedom of expression and civic space due to growing state restrictions, online intimidation, and the curtailment of academic freedom.

title: “Managing Indonesia’s Industrial Policy Bet: Capability and Competitiveness Builder or Costly Detour?” By Deasy Pane and Maria Monica Wihardja
summary: To support Indonesia’s Vision 2045, this paper argues that industrial policy must operate as a conditional, transparent performance contract to enhance competitiveness and avoid costly inefficiencies.
